blocking.issue: Figure 2 decides that a new `Stream` supersedes older streams for the same `node.id`. The published design says otherwise. Zero-downtime upgrades makes the current rule a refusal: a replica still holding the old stream answers the new `Hello` with `RZ-CP-002`, and the Node retries with full jitter. Supersession is only the proposed option of OQ-zero-downtime-upgrades-and-hot-reload-11, which Control plane and GitOps owns and has not decided. The owning document's error table matches the refusal (`RZ-CP-002`: "`node.id` taken"). The ADR therefore settles an open question silently and contradicts the Node handover sequence. L1 noted separately that supersession cannot even hold across replicas.
blocking.evidence: ADR line 100: "hello[\"Hello arrives; this Stream supersedes older ones for its node.id\"]". docs/operations/02-zero-downtime-upgrades-and-hot-reload.md line 187: "the new one takes it, dials 8091 with `Hello` and retries `RZ-CP-002` from a replica still holding the old stream with full jitter"; line 480: "| OQ-zero-downtime-upgrades-and-hot-reload-11 | Should a `Hello` with the same certificate supersede a stream ...? | (a) Supersede and keep (proposed); (b) Supersede only; (c) Neither: retry `RZ-CP-002`, pace upgrades (current) | control-plane-and-gitops | No |". docs/architecture/04-control-plane-and-gitops.md line 531: "| RZ-CP-002 | `node.id` taken, or `Hello` mismatches the certificate |"
blocking.fix: Edit only the Mermaid labels, which the word count excludes. Change `hello` to "Hello arrives". Change `ident` to "Certificate valid, unrevoked, matching Hello, and node.id on no other stream?". Change `refuse` to "RZ-CP-002 or RZ-CP-003, stream closed; the Node redials with full jitter". Optionally add OQ-zero-downtime-upgrades-and-hot-reload-11 (stream supersession) to the More information Open questions list; the 2 words L2-1 saves pay for part of it.

non_blocking.suggestion: The implicit Ack counts per (`node.id`, `storeEpoch`, `assignmentSeq`), but the owning document's `Heartbeat` row carries only digests, not `storeEpoch` or `assignmentSeq`. A `Heartbeat` therefore cannot prove which assignment it acknowledges. This is the same defect as blocking item L1-4. Resolve it through L1-4's fix: only a `Hello` that matches digest, `storeEpoch` and `assignmentSeq` counts as the Ack. Keep the proposed amendment to the owning document's `Ack` row in step with that fix.

The Delivery row says "as after a `Hello` whose Last-Known-Good or active content fails re-hash". The owning document's `Hello` has no field that reports a re-hash, and its Drift table reports a local re-hash failure as `Nack` RZ-CFG-027 followed by a `Snapshot`. Reword as "a mismatching result, like a failed local re-hash, is `Nack` RZ-CFG-027, and the next delivery is a `Snapshot`". That is also shorter. In Figure 2, change the `rehash` label to "Last Delta or re-hash NACKed RZ-CFG-027?".

Pack 8.3 defines a deterministic NACK as "an `RZ-CFG-<NNN>` error that reproduces from the Revision". The ADR's "one Ruralz Control reproduces from the Revision is deterministic (pack 8.3)" drops the `RZ-CFG` qualifier, so a reproducible non-CFG code could read as deterministic. Change it to "an `RZ-CFG` one Ruralz Control reproduces from the Revision is deterministic".

Pack 8.4 says heartbeats carry the schema level per apiVersion, and the owning document's `Heartbeat` includes `schemaLevels`. The row lists "digests, readiness and per-Rollout counters". Add "schema levels" if the word budget allows, because version skew gating (RZ-CFG-024) depends on it.

The verifier reports four WARN lines, not FAIL lines. They concern Planned (M4) relays, Planned (M3) connect ingress and grpc-go upstream, and the Planned (M2) protobuf runtime, and each has no matching roadmap item. The roadmap document must add them. The ADR's tags agree with the tech stack catalog and the pack.
